installation.note: lscpu is typically available by default as part of util-linux on most Linux distributions

overview.summary: lscpu displays information about the CPU(s) and architecture from /proc/cpuinfo and sysfs. It shows cores, threads, sockets, cache sizes, architecture, and virtualization support.
when_to_use: Check how many cores and threads the system has
See CPU architecture (x86_64, ARM, etc.) and model
Verify virtualization support (VMX, SVM) or NUMA topology

syntax.description: lscpu reads system information; no arguments are required. Options can filter or format output.

options.description: Display in extended readable format (one attribute per line)
Parseable output format; specify columns (e.g., CPU,CORE,SOCKET)

examples.title: Show CPU information
examples.description: Display architecture, cores, threads, caches, and model
examples.output:
Architecture:            x86_64
CPU(s):                8
Thread(s) per core:    2
Core(s) per socket:    4
...

examples.title: Extended format
examples.description: One attribute per line for readability

related_commands.description: Shows kernel and machine type (uname -m for arch)
